content: 1. Ethinylestradiol can reduce the effectiveness of insulin aspart due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Patients using this combination should be monitored closely, and caution is advised. 2. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, thereby reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. Diabetic patients should have their glycemic control monitored closely. 3. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of insulin degludec through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Close monitoring and caution are recommended. 4. Estrogens, including ethinylestradiol, may impair glucose tolerance. Patients should be monitored closely for any changes in glycemic control. 5. Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of insulin detemir via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 6. Oral contraceptives may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic drugs by impairing glucose tolerance. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 7. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of insulin glargine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Patients should be monitored closely, and caution is advised. 8. Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of insulin glulisine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Close monitoring and caution are recommended. 9. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of inhaled insulin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Patients should be monitored closely, and caution is advised. 10. Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of insulin lispro through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Close monitoring and caution are necessary. 11. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of insulin NPH due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Patients should be monitored closely, and caution is advised. 12. Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of regular human insulin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Close monitoring and caution are recommended. 13. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. 14. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 15. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 16. Istradefylline at 40 mg/day has been shown to increase peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. This effect was not observed with a 20 mg/day dose. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. 17. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 18. CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as itraconazole, may increase plasma hormone levels. Alternative therapies should be considered in serious cases. 19. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 20. Avoid coadministration of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates with ivosidenib, or replace with alternative therapies. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor patients for loss of therapeutic effect. 21. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 22. CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as ketoconazole, may increase plasma hormone levels. Patients should be monitored closely. 23. Ethinylestradiol decreases the levels of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 24. Combination oral contraceptives significantly decrease plasma concentrations of lamotrigine, likely due to induction of lamotrigine glucuronidation. Patients should be monitored closely. 25. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 26. Larotrectinib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 27. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 28. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended if coadministered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage modifications. 29. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 30. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel transdermal by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Patients should be monitored closely. 31. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Alternative therapies should be considered in serious cases. 32. Leniolisib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol through mechanisms involving BCRP inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 33. Leniolisib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase systemic exposure of BCRP substrates. Alternative therapies should be considered in serious cases. 34. Lesinurad decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 35. Additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods should be used when taking lesinurad. Hormonal contraception alone is not reliable. 36. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of letrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 37. Letrozole should not be given concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 38. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 40. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of liraglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 41. Oral contraceptives may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic drugs by impairing glucose tolerance. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 42. Lixisenatide decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 43. GLP-1 agonists delay gastric emptying, which may affect the absorption of concomitantly administered oral medications. Oral contraceptives should be taken at least one hour before or 11 hours after lixisenatide administration. 44. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of lomitapide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. The lomitapide dose should not exceed 30 mg/day. 45. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 46. If coadministration of lonafarnib with weak CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce or continue lonafarnib at the starting dose. Monitor closely for arrhythmias and related events, as the effect on the QT interval is unknown. 47. Ethinylestradiol decreases the levels or effects of lonapegsomatropin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 48. Oral estrogens may reduce serum insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) response to growth hormone analogs. A higher growth hormone dose may be required. 49. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 50. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels can occur with lopinavir. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 51. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 52. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable during coadministration. 53. Lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 54. Mavacamten decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 55. Mavacamten may decrease systemic exposures of ethinylestradiol and progestin, potentially leading to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Patients should use a contraceptive method unaffected by CYP450 enzyme induction or add nonhormonal contraception during coadministration and for four months after the last mavacamten dose. 56. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 57. Metronidazole decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 58. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of metyrapone through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 59. Subtherapeutic responses to metyrapone can occur in patients on estrogens, including oral contraceptives. Discontinuation of estrogens prior to and during metyrapone administration may be advisable. 60. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of mexiletine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 61. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of midazolam by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 62. Ethinylestradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, increasing serum concentrations of concomitantly administered benzodiazepines. 63. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of intranasal midazolam by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 64. Coadministration of mild CYP3A4 inhibitors with intranasal midazolam may cause higher systemic exposure, potentially prolonging sedation. 65. Mifepristone decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 66. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 67. Mineral oil decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 68. Minocycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. 69. Mitotane decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 70. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4. Monitor for possible dosage adjustments when coadministered with CYP3A4 substrates. 71. Momelotinib increases the toxicity of ethinylestradiol by plasma protein binding competition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 72. Momelotinib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase exposure to BCRP substrates, raising the risk of adverse reactions. Dose adjustments of other BCRP substrates may be necessary. 73. Moxifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 74. Mycophenolate decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol through an unknown mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 75. Patients on mycophenolate should consider using an alternative or additional form of contraception. 76. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 77. Ethinylestradiol increases the effects of naratriptan through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 78. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 79. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 80. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels can occur with nelfinavir. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 81. Nemolizumab decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended.
